findings.summary: The 17-position assembly-order comment presents itself as the order for all variants, but Physics and Histogram emit addHeader() output (position 3) AFTER Coloring (position 6) instead of before Math — and Physics is documented as '1-10' when it never emits position 10 at all.
findings.change: Rewrote the variant footnote. Physics is now stated as 1-9 plus a simplified inline trace, with position 10 explicitly called out as absent, and a CAVEAT paragraph records that the numbered list is the MAIN template's order verbatim: headers and the Math/BlueNoise/Coloring chunks see each other in opposite orders depending on variant, so anything richer than a #define added via addHeader must be checked against both orderings. Notes that today's sole caller, materials.ts MAIN_HEADER, is preprocessor-only and injected for every non-Mesh variant, which is why the divergence is latent rather than live.
findings.verification: Read the three return templates in buildFragment() directly. Main emits `${defines} ${uniforms} ${headers} ${math} ${BLUE_NOISE} ${COLORING} ${preambles}`; Physics and Histogram both emit `${defines} ${uniforms} ${math} ${BLUE_NOISE} ${COLORING} ${headers} ${preambles}` — headers move from position 3 to position 7. The Physics template's chunk list stops at ${de} followed by simplifiedTraceGLSL with no ${postDEFunctions}, while Histogram does emit it — so 'Physics variant: 1-10' was off by one. MAIN_HEADER contains only #ifdef/#define, confirming latency; its inject gates only on variant === 'Mesh', so it reaches all three affected templates. smoke:engine-gmt is the behavioural guard — it boots app-gmt.html and compiles a real Mandelbulb (54ms) through this exact builder — but it cannot fail on a comment change, which is the honest limit here; the claim is proved by the template text.

findings.summary: ShaderBuilder.addUniform carried no contract at all, despite being the one API where a stray call is a hard GL compile failure rather than a silent overwrite — this builder appends to an already-complete declaration block, so re-adding an existing name emits a duplicate `uniform …;` line.
findings.change: Added a three-clause @invariant: (1) keyed on name alone with Map.set last-wins, deliberately weaker than UniformSchema's module-load throw, which cannot see builder-time calls from inject(); (2) the GMT-specific duplicate-declaration hazard, naming both static prefixes and the two legitimate uses (the backingOnly R10 pattern and the Mesh variant); (3) neither emit site checks backingOnly, which is honoured only by engine-gmt/shaders/chunks/uniforms.ts. Committed with the addHeader finding — same file.
findings.verification: Read both emit sites: buildUniformsString() starts `let out = UNIFORMS + '\n'` then appends the map; buildMeshSDFLibrary() interpolates ${injectedUniforms} after ${MESH_GLSL_UNIFORMS} plus a hardcoded stub list. Neither reads backingOnly. The duplicate-declaration consequence needed NO probe — engine-gmt/features/weave.ts:142-155 already gates its entire addUniform loop on `variant === 'Mesh'` and states the consequence in the codebase's own words ('declaring here too would be a GLSL redefinition error, hence the gate'). The only two addUniform callers repo-wide are that one and core_math.ts:109 (the backingOnly uModularParams case), matching the documented legitimate uses exactly. That in-source corroboration is stronger than the probe the salvaged diff claimed to have run, and cost nothing.

findings.summary: The syncFrame step-ordering @invariant claimed 'lights need uCameraPosition zeroed first' — an ordering dependency that does not exist, since the light block never reads that uniform.
findings.change: Removed the clause and replaced it with an explicit negative note: the light block packs positions camera-relative itself via VirtualSpace.getLightShaderVector, which subtracts camera.position and the scene offset directly, so the set(0,0,0) may sit anywhere in the method. Also recorded that FractalEngine.syncCameraFromMatrix writes a NON-zero uCameraPosition on the worker's boot camera sync. The two genuine ordering constraints are left intact.
findings.verification: Grepped uCameraPosition across the whole method: within UniformManager.ts it appears only in the invariant text and at the set(0,0,0) write; the light block reads lighting.lights, modulations, cam and virtualSpace and nothing else. Read VirtualSpace.getLightShaderVector to close the indirection — it uses camera.quaternion / camera.position and this.offset, never a uniform. This also REFUTES the reason the dying cycle-6 agent gave ('one writer repo-wide, unconditionally zero'): there are THREE writers — UniformManager.ts:335 (zero), WorkerHistogram.ts:73 (zero), and FractalEngine.ts:461 (a real camera translation, called from renderWorker on initialCamera). The clause is still wrong, but for a different reason than it believed — which is exactly why the salvaged diff was treated as a lead rather than committed.
